narrative.overview: PurseInator looks like a warm room in late-afternoon light where someone sits with a box of belongings and discovers, slowly, what they love most. The work is affirmation, not subtraction — recognizing the things that matter, with letting go following naturally from that clarity. The reference is Cabana magazine in print — cozy, intimate, maximalist, materially rich — not the flat tech-product look and not Cabana's own thin website. The maximalism is rehomed as affection: it lives in the user's photographs, the warm parchment palette and its jewel-tone content, and the old-style serif voice, never in the density of the interface. The chrome stays quiet so exactly one loving choice is ever in front of the person sorting. The system rejects every frame that treats belongings as stock: not a catalog, not an inventory tool, not a shopping site, and never a gamified declutter app, a resale-marketplace listing, or an enterprise asset dashboard.
keyCharacteristics: Warm honey-parchment light theme; pure white and cool gray are forbidden.
Achromatic espresso-ink chrome; gilt-gold warmth as garnish; color lives in the content.
Editorial serif (Fraunces) for soul; humanist sans (Hanken Grotesk) for everything functional.
Calm density: one decision at a time, generous but cozy spacing.
Flat tonal layering with one soft, warm lift; gentle 150-250ms motion.

rules.name: The Achromatic-Chrome Rule
rules.body: No hue is spent on the interface itself — buttons, the title, links, focus, and progress are espresso ink. Color belongs to the content (photographs and covers), and that restraint is what makes the current decision unmistakable.

rules.name: The Gilt-as-Garnish Rule
rules.body: Gold is seasoning, never substance. It may warm a badge, an illustration, or an empty-state mark; it may never be a button you press or a state that warns you.

rules.name: The No Cold Surface Rule
rules.body: Every surface is warm — Vellum or Veil. Pure #ffffff and any cool/blue-tinted gray are prohibited; they break the room instantly.

rules.name: The Serif-for-Soul, Sans-for-Sense Rule
rules.body: Fraunces appears only where feeling belongs — names of things, headings, the item being decided. Every dense, functional, or repeated string is Hanken Grotesk. Fraunces in a UI label is a bug.

rules.name: The Fixed-Scale Rule
rules.body: Type sizes are a fixed rem scale, never fluid clamp(). This is product UI viewed at consistent distance.

rules.name: The Paper-on-a-Warm-Table Rule
rules.body: Shadows are warm (tinted with Ink, never pure black) and soft. A hard, dark, tight drop shadow reads as a 2014 app.

dos: Do frame the work as affirmation — 'which do you love more?' — not as culling. Copy and motion celebrate favorites; letting go is honored quietly, never the headline.
Do keep one decision in view at a time; let whitespace and pacing carry the calm.
Do let the user's photographs be the loudest, richest thing on the screen.
Do keep the chrome achromatic — espresso ink for buttons, links, focus, and progress; let color live in the content.
Do keep all surfaces warm (Vellum/Veil) and all text warm Ink — verify body text ≥4.5:1.
Do reserve Fraunces for names, headings, and the item being decided; Hanken for everything functional.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion with a crossfade or instant transition on every animation.
Do support tap-first interaction with ≥44px targets; drag is allowed for reordering/bucketing.
donts: Don't make this a catalog, an inventory/storage tool, or a shopping site — no dense SKU grids, no stock counts, no cart/'add more' affordances.
Don't evoke Marie Kondo-style gamified declutter apps, Poshmark/eBay selling UIs, or enterprise asset-management dashboards.
Don't gamify letting go: no confetti, streaks, points, scores-as-rewards, or 'you have too many.'
Don't use #ffffff, cool/blue grays, or fire-engine semantic colors — they shatter the lamplit warmth.
Don't ship Cabana's thin website energy: the richness is cozy and material, not sparse-and-trendy.
Don't distinguish buckets or states by hue alone; always pair with label, icon, or position.
Don't use fluid clamp() heading scales, hard black drop shadows, or border-left color stripes.
